A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same curriculum-learning work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original convergence experiments, image-generation benchmarks, ablations, and qualitative results in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendices F-G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds longer-training comparisons, DiT-XL results, and convergence analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same timestep clustering, easy-to-hard task accumulation, loss-based pacing, and subsequent training across all timesteps. Algorithms 1 and 2 are unchanged; the additional experiments do not modify the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover unconditional FFHQ generation, class-conditional CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation, and MS-COCO text-to-image generation. The new ImageNet convergence analysis reuses existing dataset and task coverage; longer training and larger models add settings.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla, NaiveCL, curriculum and anti-curriculum variants, MinSNR, and DTR. The added longer-training and larger-model comparisons use the existing Vanilla-versus-Ours pairing. Newly discussed related methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds quantitative evaluation at 2M iterations, extends the model-size comparison to DiT-XL/2, and introduces a loss-oscillation convergence diagnostic. v2 already included qualitative samples from 2M-iteration training. Appendix B also changes EDM's stated budget from '4,000 iterations' to '4,000 kimg iterations' while retaining '1 million images'; this inconsistent wording does not establish an actual training-budget change.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds SiT stabilization-point analysis and an ImageNet replication of timestep-dependent loss convergence. The longer-training and DiT-XL comparisons further test persistence of the curriculum benefit. Existing clustering, pacing, model-size, and noise-schedule analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run summaries, seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The Monte Carlo estimation procedure is unchanged; v3's newly disclosed image count documents its implementation without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained table scores are unchanged. v3 Table 2 adds 2M-iteration FID values of 7.84 for Vanilla and 6.24 for Ours. Table 4 adds DiT-XL/2 results, including FID 9.40 versus 7.57 and recall 0.49 versus 0.48. Appendix B adds stabilization and ImageNet convergence findings. These are additional results under additional settings.

T1.justification: The SDE formulation, training objective, KL definitions, and Monte Carlo estimators in Equations (1)-(5) remain unchanged. Appendix C expands an informal explanation of numerical instability without adding a formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract is identical, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: smaller-timestep denoising is harder, and difficulty-based curriculum training improves generation and convergence while remaining compatible with existing techniques. The new experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly attributes near-zero-timestep KL instability to narrow support, distributional non-overlap, and zero densities. Section 6.2 interprets the longer-training comparison as evidence of robustness. The limitations paragraph is unchanged, moving from Appendix I to J.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses that 5,000 images were sampled for KL approximation; v2 supplied only the estimator formulas. Appendix B describes the new convergence-point measurement. Existing optimizer, learning rate, batch size, EMA, precision, and eight-A100 hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 distinguishes the approach from progressive distillation and cascaded diffusion. New Appendix H explains its distinction from Go et al.'s task-affinity and negative-transfer work, adding Fifty et al. as context. Appendix C adds supporting citations for its distributional discussion. These are focused extensions of the existing positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adopts author-year citations, updates publication and author-affiliation information, subdivides Appendix A, and adds focused experimental and discussion paragraphs. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 2 and Appendix Figures A-B, expands the model-size table with XL rows, and adopts ICLR headers and typography. Existing displays are repositioned and renumbered, including regrouping qualitative panels. The original plots and sample images are retained.

improvement.justification: The matched 2M-iteration comparison adds quantitative support beyond v2's qualitative samples, while DiT-XL results and the ImageNet convergence analysis strengthen validation of scalability and the central observation. Added positioning and the KL sample count also improve documentation. These are incremental gains: the new KL-instability explanation remains unvalidated, and Appendix B introduces inconsistent EDM-budget units, but the additional comparative evidence provides a limited net improvement.
